The code deliberately collects .env-like files and parses environment keys/values, then exfiltrates that data to an external URL. The destination URL is hidden as a base64 string (Indicator 1/2) which decodes to an external cloudfunctions endpoint, and the HTTP request is obscured via __import__ + getattr and lambda wrappers (Indicator 3). This is targeted data exfiltration of potentially sensitive secrets and credentials — clearly malicious behavior.

The code posts a sensitive value (private_key) to a hard-coded external endpoint and then polls a remote "switcher" URL to decide behavior. That is classic data exfiltration + remote control (C2) behavior. Even if mockapi.io is a test service, the intent to send private keys and use a remote switch makes this malicious rather than benign/test code.

The code reads .env-like files, collects environment key/value pairs, then exfiltrates them to an external URL. The URL is hidden as a base64 string (decoded to something like https://us-central1-...cloudfunctions.net/submit), the network call is dynamically imported/constructed (__import__("requests"), getattr(..., "get"), lambdas), and the payload is sent as a JSON query parameter. These are clear, deliberate obfuscation techniques combined with data exfiltration of potentially sensitive secrets — behavior that is malicious.
